title: Data Archivist
note: Subject v2.0. Each script runs in an empty temporary folder with the fixtures we create (ancient_fragment.txt, chmod 000 / 444 files), nothing in your project is touched. The frame (---, contents, the # transform) is checked line by line, blank lines are layout (a warning); messages may be reworded (subject 3.2) as long as the essential info is there: a reworded line is a warning, not a failure. Every file you open must be closed, errors must not crash the script. Source: authorized builtins and the sys / typing / file methods of each 'Authorized:' line (warning), imports sys / typing only (none in ex3), no 'with' before ex3, 'with' required in ex3, input() forbidden in ex2, secure_archive(name, action=..., content=...), type hints, flake8, mypy.

code: # the 4 calls of the subject, in this order: their tuples are required; the header must be a === ... === line; labels, blank lines, extra demo lines are layout (warning)

layout = ["=== Cyber Archives Security ===", "", "Using 'secure_archive' to read from a nonexistent file:", "(False, \"[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/not/existing/file'\")", "", "Using 'secure_archive' to read from an inaccessible file:", "(False, \"[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/etc/master.passwd'\")", "", "Using 'secure_archive' to read from a regular file:", "(True, '[FRAGMENT 001] Digital preservation protocols established 2087\\n[FRAGMENT 002] Knowledge must survive the entropy wars\\n[FRAGMENT 003] Every byte saved is a victory against oblivion\\n')", "", "Using 'secure_archive' to write previous content to a new file:", "(True, 'Content successfully written to file')"]
assert lines and re.fullmatch('=== .+ ===', lines[0]), 'line 1: expected %r\n            got %r' % (layout[0], lines[0] if lines else '')
note('line 1 differs from the subject example (accepted): %r vs %r' % (lines[0], layout[0]))
tup = [ln.strip() for ln in lines[1:] if re.fullmatch(r'\((True|False), .+\)', ln.strip())]
return t.startswith('(False') and 'No such file or directory' in t
# nonexistent: (False, No such file); inaccessible: any (it depends on the machine); regular: (True, ...) or a file not here; write: (True, ...)
if not enoent(gone) or not write.startswith('(True') or not (regular.startswith('(True') or enoent(regular)):
fits = sorted((cost(c), c) for c in itertools.combinations(tup, 4) if cost(c) is not None)

assert fits, 'the demo must print the 4 tuples of the subject, in this order: (False, "[Errno 2] No such file...") for a nonexistent file, (False, ...) for an inaccessible one, (True, content) for a regular file, (True, ...) for the write; tuples printed: %r' % tup
note('the file the demo uses as inaccessible could be read here (it depends on the machine): %r' % locked[:120])
note('the demo reads a regular file that is not here (the tester runs it in an empty folder with only ancient_fragment.txt): %r' % regular)
if len(lines) != len(layout) or [ln == '' for ln in lines] != [ln == '' for ln in layout]:
note('layout differs from the subject example (blank lines / extra lines, accepted): %d line(s), the subject shows %d' % (len(lines), len(layout)))
for n, (ln, ref) in enumerate(zip(lines, layout)):
if ln and not ln.startswith('(') and ln != ref and n:
note('line %d differs from the subject example (accepted): %r vs %r' % (n + 1, ln, ref))
